title: Performance reviews and what they measure

turns.speaker: Doug
turns.text: We're dropping the annual review and the rating scale with it. Quarterly conversations instead, no number attached.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Which sounds lovely until pay day, when somebody still has to decide who gets what.

turns.speaker: Pia
turns.text: That's the honest problem with abolishing ratings. The judgement doesn't disappear, it just stops being written down.

turns.speaker: Doug
turns.text: Is that worse? At least nobody carries a three around for a year.

turns.speaker: Pia
turns.text: It's worse for anyone who wants to challenge it. You can appeal a rating. You can't appeal a vibe.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: And the bias research points the same way. Unstructured judgement is where it flourishes.

turns.speaker: Doug
turns.text: The forced distribution version was indefensible, though. Ten per cent must be underperforming, by decree.

turns.speaker: Pia
turns.text: Completely, and several large firms dropped it after finding it destroyed exactly the collaboration they said they wanted.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Because helping a colleague moves them up your own curve.

turns.speaker: Pia
turns.text: Roughly. Specific criteria, written evidence, more than one assessor, and no quota.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: The part nobody fixes is that most of it measures whether your manager saw the work rather than whether the work was good.

turns.speaker: Doug
turns.text: Which is why the people who present well keep doing extremely well.

points: A company is replacing annual reviews and ratings with quarterly conversations.
Pia warns that removing ratings does not remove judgement, only the record of it.
This disadvantages anyone wishing to challenge a decision, since an unwritten judgement cannot be appealed.
Bias research indicates unstructured judgement increases bias.
Forced distribution systems are rejected as destroying collaboration, since helping colleagues harms one's own ranking.
They favour structured but unranked assessment, while noting reviews largely measure managerial visibility rather than work quality.
